# An explicit small-endpoint necessity from a whole swept segment

This is a necessary condition for a hypothetical bad source in the
actual planar proper-A, zero-B three-cap regime. It is not a general
mixed-integer depth theorem. It combines two geometric statements about
the same fibers: the shifted three-direction cover on A and the whole
segment swept through B. Neither input is an independent marginal menu.

## 1. Exact scope and elementary cap profiles

Put

    v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(-1,-1),
    T={x:v_i.x<=1},                 |T|=9/2.

Let A,K,B be planar convex bodies with (A+B)/2 subset K and B subset T.
Work with exactly the three-fiber mixed set

    S=({-1} times A) union ({0} times K) union ({1} times B),

with no additional integer fibers contributing area. Its raw halfspace
depth at(0,0) is the infimum of the sums of the three captured areas
over all closed ambient halfspaces containing(0,0). Assume0 is interior
to K and each ambient cap

    H_i={(z,x):v_i.x>=z}

attains this source's genuine raw depth Q.
Every A cut at level -1 is proper and every B capture at level 1 has
area zero. Write a=|A|, k=|K|, b=|B|, and suppose

    b<=a+k,                Q<=(2/9)(a+k+b).             (1)

The first conclusion proved below is

    a<b/5.                                                (2)

The actual additive area reserve in the swept-segment theorem further
sharpens it to

    a/b < (80-30sqrt(3))/153 <3/16.                        (2a)

Retaining the whole-A lower-tail height, Section5 further proves the
stronger simple conclusion

    a<b/6.                                                (2b)

Sort the three captured A areas as u<=v<=w, and denote the normal of
the largest cap by v_l. Define

    q=Q-w, delta=a-u-v, r=delta/w, x=u/w,
    delta_*=delta+3u/4, theta=delta_*/w,
    h=h_A(v_l), H=h+1.

The standard positive-part ordinary cap-cover inequality gives

    a<=w+v+u/4,
    k<=(9/4)Q-u-v-w/4.                                (3)

Its complete proof by sequential parallel trimming and the ordinary
Grunbaum inequality is in
`candidate eb88c1c4c388daab`.
Combining (1) and (3), as in the all-level source, gives

    delta>=w/4>0,
    b>=(9/4)q+(5/2-r)w.                               (4)

The three halfplanes v_i.x>=-1 cover the whole plane, so (3) applies
to A; the middle traces through 0 cover the whole plane as well.
All these measures are ordinary area, so their boundary lines are null.

## 2. A proved cross-direction tail and the whole swept segment

The two smaller A caps, together with the shifted cap v_l.x>=2,
also cover the whole plane: their three thresholds sum to zero.
Write tau for the shifted cap area. Applying the same ordinary cover
inequality gives

    tau>=delta+(3/4)min(u,tau).

Since delta>=w/4>=u/4, the possibility tau<u would imply
tau>=4delta>=u, a contradiction. Therefore

    tau>=delta_* >0.                                  (5)

Thus h>2, since a level line has zero area. In particular H>3 before
the following contraction is made.

The original largest cap D=A intersect {v_l.x>=-1} has area w and
height H. Contract D toward an actual point on its level -1 by
factor 3/H. The image lies below level 2 and has area 9w/H^2.
Using (5),

    H>=3/sqrt(1-theta),       1/4<=r<=theta<1.          (6)

The strict upper bound theta<1 follows because the original cut is
proper and every intermediate section below level 2 has positive
length. These facts also show h>2 and H>3.

For completeness, the weaker whole-segment estimate used here has
a short direct proof. Relabel the normal coordinates so t=v_l.x=-X-Y.
Choose two actual points of A attaining its t minimum l<-1 and maximum
h>2. The segment joining them lies in A. An area-preserving shear
s=X-c t makes this segment vertical; it has constant s=s_A.
For each transverse coordinate s of B, write its actual t section as
[L(s),U(s)]. Since B subset T,

    -2<=L(s)<=U(s)<=1.

The section of segment+B at s_A+s is [l+L(s),h+U(s)]. It straddles
0, so its portion in t>=0 has length h+U(s). Midpoint containment
therefore gives

    4q>=integral (h+U(s)) ds.

Pointwise,

    h+U-H(U-L)/3
       =[(h-2)(1-U)+H(L+2)]/3>=0.

Integrating with determinant-one coordinates proves

    b<=12q/H.                                         (7)

The sharper roof-capacity theorem and its exact coordinate proof are
in `candidate cde78a6346699a8a`.
No existence of a minimizing shape is used in (7).

## 3. Exact scalar elimination preserving the geometric coupling

Combining (4) and (7),

    (5/2-r)w <= b[1-3H/16]
              <=b[1-9/(16sqrt(1-theta))].             (8)

Its left side is positive: r<=theta<1 and w>0. Consequently, with
s=sqrt(1-theta),

    9/16<s<=sqrt(3)/2.

Since v<=w and x=(4/3)(theta-r),

    a/w=r+x+v/w<=1+(4/3)theta-r/3.

For each fixed theta, the ratio

    [1+(4/3)theta-r/3]/(5/2-r)

is increasing in r: its derivative is
[1/6+(4/3)theta]/(5/2-r)^2>0. As r<=theta, (8) yields

    a/b <= g(s)
         =(2-s^2)[1-9/(16s)]/(3/2+s^2).              (9)

This estimate keeps theta=delta_*/w throughout; replacing it by the
unshifted residual fraction would lose the conclusion below.

To prove g(s)<1/5 exactly, subtract and clear its positive denominator:

    1/5-g(s)
       =[96s^3-45s^2-136s+90]/[40s(2s^2+3)].

Put z=s-7/8. Since s>9/16, z>-5/16, and the numerator is

    z^2(207+96z)+(23/4)z+55/64
      >=177z^2+(23/4)z+55/64>0.

The last quadratic is strictly positive because its leading coefficient
is positive and its discriminant equals -9206/16<0. This proves (2).

## 4. The additive whole-body reserve gives a stronger explicit split

Section4 of
`candidate cde78a6346699a8a` proves
the strengthened swept-set estimate

    4q>=Hb/3+tau>=Hb/3+theta w.                       (10)

Its reserve comes from the two distinct boundary gains when the actual
A body replaces its extreme segment in A+B. After shearing that
segment vertical, write actual A sections as [a_-(t),a_+(t)] with
a_-<=0<=a_+. A rightmost point of B adds the full positive boundary
gain a_+(t) for t>=2, and a leftmost point adds -a_-(t). Each endpoint
height of B lies in [-2,1], so both gains occur above the tested level0.
Their separate boundary-width contributions add even if the longitudinal
ranges overlap; their sum integrates to tau. Thus (10) retains actual
disjoint area increments, not an assumed sum of overlapping subsets.

Combining (10) with (4) now gives

    [5/2-r+(9/16)theta]w
       <=b[1-3H/16]
       <=b[1-9/(16sqrt(1-theta))].                    (11)

For fixed theta, the ratio

    [1+(4/3)theta-r/3]/[5/2+(9/16)theta-r]

increases strictly in r, because its derivative has positive numerator
1/6+(55/48)theta. Since u>0, we have r<theta, so (11) implies

    a/b < G(s)
        =(2-s^2)(16s-9)/[s(33+7s^2)],
    9/16<s<=sqrt(3)/2.                               (12)

The derivative of G is -P(s)/[s^2(7s^2+33)^2], where

    P(s)=63s^4+1504s^3-675s^2-594.

On the interval in (12),

    P'(s)=s[252s^2+4512s-1350]>0:

the bracket is increasing and its value at9/16 is81135/64>0.
Moreover

    P(sqrt(3)/2)=564sqrt(3)-17037/16<0,

as sqrt(3)<7/4 and 564(7/4)=15792/16<17037/16. Thus G is
strictly increasing on the whole relevant interval. Evaluating its
upper endpoint gives

    G(s)<=G(sqrt(3)/2)=(80-30sqrt(3))/153.

Finally this number is less than3/16 because 821<480sqrt(3),
which follows by squaring the positive sides:
821^2=674041<691200=3(480)^2. This proves (2a) exactly.

The bound (2a) does not optimize away any source into a point outside
the mixed set; it is solely a necessary restriction on the volumes
of the actual two endpoint fibers under (1).

## 5. Retaining the whole-A extension improves the split to one sixth

Put alpha=a/w>1. The strict inequality follows because the original
largest A cut is proper. Lower-cap square-root concavity on the same
body A at longitudinal levels -1,2,h gives

    sqrt(a-delta_*)
       >=sqrt(a-w)+(3/H)[sqrt(a)-sqrt(a-w)].

Indeed the lower cap at2 has area at most a-delta_* by (5), whereas
its square root is at least the linear interpolation of the lower-cap
roots at -1 and h. Thus

    H>=J(alpha,theta)
      :=3[ sqrt(alpha)-sqrt(alpha-1) ]
           /[ sqrt(alpha-theta)-sqrt(alpha-1) ].     (13)

The denominator is positive because theta<1. This is the whole-A
height bound; it preserves alpha and theta jointly. Equations(11)
and(13) imply

    a/b <= alpha N(alpha,theta)/D(r,theta),
    N=1-(3/16)J,
    D=5/2-r+(9/16)theta.                            (14)

The right side is positive at every admissible bad configuration.
The original variables satisfy

    r>=1/4,
    theta>=r,
    theta>=(3/4)(alpha-1)+r/4.                       (15)

The last inequality is precisely v/w<=1, since
alpha=r+(4/3)(theta-r)+v/w. We will maximize a relaxation of
(14) using only (15), so any additional actual constraints are retained
by implication rather than presumed attainable.

Here are the derivative facts needed for an exact elimination. For
alpha>1 and0<theta<1, set

    e=sqrt(alpha-1), X=sqrt(alpha), Y=sqrt(alpha-theta).

Differentiating the displayed radical formula gives

    J_alpha/J=[1/Y-1/X]/(2e)>0,
    J_theta/J=(1+e/Y)/[2(1-theta)].                  (16)

Also J>=3/sqrt(1-theta). Hence for theta>=1/4,

    J>=2sqrt(3),             J_theta>=3/2.

If additionally alpha>=5/4, then e/Y>=1/2, because
3alpha+theta>=4. In this range (16) gives the stronger

    J_theta>=J.                                     (17)

For fixed alpha and r, the right side of (14) decreases with theta:
its positive numerator decreases and its positive denominator increases.
We may therefore replace theta by

    theta_0=max{r,(3/4)(alpha-1)+r/4}.               (18)

This replacement leaves N positive. On each of the two pieces of
(18), the resulting quotient also decreases with r, as follows.

On the piece theta_0=r, its derivative has the sign of

    -3J_theta D+7N.

Here D>=33/16 and J_theta>=3/2, while N<=1. Thus
3J_theta D>=297/32>7>=7N, so the derivative is negative.

On the piece theta_0=(3/4)(alpha-1)+r/4, we have alpha>=1+r>=5/4.
The derivative now has the sign of

    -3J_theta D+55N.

Using (17), D>=33/16, and N=1-3J/16,

    3J_theta D-55N
       >=(33/2)J-55
       >=33sqrt(3)-55>0.

The last inequality follows from sqrt(3)>5/3. Thus this derivative
is negative as well. At the meeting point the two expressions are
continuous. Reducing r to1/4 can only increase the relaxed bound.
Consequently it suffices to consider

    r=1/4,
    theta_0=max{1/4,3alpha/4-11/16}.                (19)

For1<alpha<=5/4, theta_0=1/4 and D=153/64. Split this interval
at alpha=9/8. When alpha<=9/8, use J>=2sqrt(3) to obtain

    alpha N/D <=(8-3sqrt(3))/17<1/6.               (20)

The strict comparison is equivalent to31<18sqrt(3), verified by
31^2=961<972=3(18)^2. When9/8<=alpha<=5/4, monotonicity in alpha
from(16) and direct evaluation give

    J(alpha,1/4)>=J(9/8,1/4)=1+sqrt(7).

Thus

    alpha N/D <=[65-15sqrt(7)]/153<1/6.            (21)

The strict comparison is equivalent to79<30sqrt(7), verified by
79^2=6241<6300=7(30)^2.

It remains to control alpha>=5/4 on the other piece of(19). There

    theta_0=3alpha/4-11/16,
    D=(477+108alpha)/256,        D'=27/64.

As long as N is positive, J_alpha+(3/4)J_theta>=(3/4)J by(16)--(17),
so along this curve N'<=-9J/64. Differentiating alpha N/D, its numerator
is bounded above by

    N(D-alpha D')-(9/64)alpha J D.

Use D-alpha D'=477/256, N<=1/2, alpha>=5/4, J>=3, and D>=9/4.
The resulting upper bound is

    477/512-1215/1024=-261/1024<0.

The quotient therefore decreases from its value at alpha=5/4, which
is already strictly below1/6 by(21). If N becomes nonpositive,
(14) is incompatible with a/b>0, so that range cannot occur.
This proves (2b) for every actual configuration in the stated scope.

## 6. Two positive residual intersections force a still smaller endpoint

Suppose additionally

    a-u-w>0.                                         (22)

Then in fact

    a<b/9.                                          (23)

Here is the extra actual geometry, including its strictness. Denote the
normals of u,v,w by v_i,v_j,v_l respectively. Positive area of the two
open residual intersections supplies actual points

    P in A with v_i.P<-1 and v_l.P<-1,
    R in A with v_i.R<-1 and v_j.R<-1.

Their existence follows by inclusion-exclusion: the first intersection
has area at least a-u-w>0, and the second has area at least delta>0.
Since the three normals sum to zero,

    v_j.P>2,              v_j.R<-1.

The entire segment E=[P,R] lies in A intersect {v_i.x<-1}, and its
v_j-coordinate span D is strictly greater than3. Adding B preserves
the strict missed inequality, because B subset {v_i.x<=1}. Therefore

    (E+B)/2 subset K intersect {v_i.x<0}.

Use t=v_j.x as longitudinal coordinate and a determinant-one shear
making E vertical. Let W_B>0 be the transverse projection length of B.
The exact segment extrusion formula and B's t-coordinate span at most3
give

    |E+B|=b+D W_B> b+3W_B>=2b.

The last inequality is Fubini: every B section along that segment
direction has t-length at most3, so b<=3W_B. The tested middle cap
has area Q-u. Thus

    k-Q+u>b/2.                                       (24)

This is a missed-region estimate, distinct from the captured swept-set
reserve used earlier.

Let F=u+v+w/4. The middle profile implies Q>=(4/9)(k+F).
Together with(24) it gives

    k>(9/10)b-u+(4/5)v+w/5.

On the other hand, combining the bad target with the middle profile
gives k<=a+b-2F. Comparing these two bounds and using a-u-v=rw,

    b/10>(7/10-r)w+(9/5)v.                           (25)

Write x=u/w and y=v/w. Assumption(22) says y>1-r. Also r<=theta
and positivity in(11) gives theta<175/256. Consequently every
denominator below is positive. Rearranging(25),

    a/b < (r+x+y)/(7-10r+18y)
         <=(1+x)/(25-28r).                           (26)

For the second inequality, the derivative of the middle expression
with respect to y has numerator 7-28r-18x<=0, because r>=1/4.
Thus lowering y to1-r only increases that expression.

If theta<=4/7, then x=(4/3)(theta-r) and r<=theta imply

    28r+9x=16r+12theta<=28theta<=16.

Equivalently, 9(1+x)<=25-28r, so(26) proves(23).

If theta>=4/7, the strictly increasing function G from(12) gives

    a/b<G(sqrt(3/7))<1/9.

For the last comparison, direct substitution gives

    G(sqrt(3/7))=[176-99/sqrt(3/7)]/252.

It is less than1/9 precisely when sqrt(3/7)<99/148. Squaring
positive sides reduces this to

    3(148)^2=65712<68607=7(99)^2.

This proves(23) throughout the additional regime(22), using two
actual residual intersections of the same endpoint body.

## 7. A disjoint actual missed-body reserve improves one ninth to one twelfth

The normal-cone injection proved in Section6 of
`candidate 5fcdb1b3fadb0891` supplies
one additional disjoint region. In the setting of Section6 above,
take E=A intersect {v_i.x<-1}, where i is the smallest-cap normal.
Its area is a-u. The actual residual segment lies in one affine line,
which has zero area. The injection translates pieces of E by actual
points of B into the shared strict missed region, outside the cylinder
generated by that line and B. These images are disjoint from the
entire swept segment+B. Therefore(24) strengthens to

    k-Q+u>b/2+(a-u)/4.                               (27)

No overlapping added copies are counted. The referenced result proves
the injection by a deterministic finite support-point partition and
continuity from below on the source sets, including the required
original-cylinder avoidance.

Combining(27) with Q>=(4/9)(k+F) gives

    k>(9/10)b+(9/20)a-(29/20)u+(4/5)v+w/5.

Compare again with k<=a+b-2F and substitute a-u-v=rw. The result is

    b>(7-11r/2)w+(45/2)v.                            (28)

With x=u/w and y=v/w>1-r, the same monotonicity argument now gives

    a/b<(r+x+y)/(7-11r/2+45y/2)
         <=(1+x)/(59/2-28r).                        (29)

The derivative with respect to y has numerator7-28r-(45/2)x<=0;
all denominators are positive since r<175/256. If theta<=5/8,

    28r+12x=12r+16theta<=28theta<=35/2,

so12(1+x)<=59/2-28r. Equation(29) then yields a/b<1/12.
If theta>=5/8, use instead the increasing G from Section4:

    a/b<G(sqrt(3/8))=[208-117/sqrt(3/8)]/285<1/12.

The last comparison is equivalent to sqrt(3/8)<468/737, and squaring
positive sides gives the exact certificate

    3(737)^2=1629507<1752192=8(468)^2.

Thus every configuration with the extra two-residual hypothesis(22)
in fact satisfies

    a<b/12.                                         (30)

This conclusion combines one common swept set with one independently
proved disjoint reserve of the actual missed part of A. It does not
assume disjointness of several swept sets.

## 8. Disjoint whole residual bodies improve one twelfth to one thirty-second

Retain the extra two-residual hypothesis (22), namely a-u-w>0.
Let i,j,l be respectively the smallest, middle, and largest captured
A indices. The two ACTUAL unique-capture regions R_l and R_j obey

    |R_l|>=a-u-v=rw,
    |R_j|>=a-u-w=(r+y-1)w>0,        y=v/w.            (31)

The complete all-dimensional proof in
`candidate cf1b9ba5ada0a5ef` applies
Brunn--Minkowski to each WHOLE residual body and B. Their midpoint sums
lie in disjoint unique middle sectors, both missing the i-th cap.
Consequently

    k-Q+u >= b/2+(2r+y-1)w/4
                 +(sqrt(bw)/2)(sqrt(r)+sqrt(r+y-1)).  (32)

This uses a genuine disjointness argument for these two sets. It does
not add (32) to the previous swept-segment or normal-cone reserves.

The upper profile k<=(9/4)Q-u-v-w/4 and the target consequence

    Q<=(4/9)(a+b-u-v-w/4)
      =4b/9+(4r-1)w/9

give

    k-Q+u <=5b/9+[(10r-7)/18-y]w.

Put z=w/b>0 and compare with (32). The result, with all square-root
credits retained, is

    2 >= (5-2r+45y)z
           +18sqrt(z)(sqrt(r)+sqrt(r+y-1)).           (33)

The established parameter bounds are

    r>=1/4, y>1-r, y<=1,
    theta=r+3x/4<175/256, x=u/w>0,
    a/b=(r+x+y)z.                                    (34)

The strict theta bound follows already from positivity on the left of
(11): 1-9/[16sqrt(1-theta)]>0. We now prove from (33)--(34) that

    a<b/32.                                         (35)

Suppose instead that a/b>=1/32. Write alpha=r+x+y. Then
z>=1/(32alpha). Both terms on the right of (33) increase with z;
their linear coefficient is positive, since
5-2r+45y>50-47r>0. Thus (33) would imply

    2 >= (5-2r+45y)/(32alpha)
       +18(sqrt(r)+sqrt(r+y-1))/sqrt(32alpha).        (36)

For fixed r,y the right side decreases as x increases. We can enlarge
x to x_bar=(4/3)(175/256-r), a strictly positive number. Next, with
x=x_bar fixed, that right side increases with y on 1-r<=y<=1.
For its first term the derivative has positive numerator

    45(r+x_bar+y)-(5-2r+45y)
      =47r+45x_bar-5>0.

For the square-root term, put t=r+y-1>=0. For t>0 its derivative has
the sign of

    (r+x_bar+y)-sqrt(rt)-t
      =1+x_bar-sqrt(rt)>0,

because 0<t<=r<1. Continuity handles t=0. We may therefore lower y
to 1-r in (36). Set

    A(r)=1+x_bar=367/192-(4/3)r,
    f(r)=(50-47r)/(32A(r))+18sqrt(r/(32A(r))).

Equation (36) implies 2>=f(r). But f is strictly increasing throughout
1/4<=r<175/256. Indeed, with c=367/192,

    32 A(r)^2 f'(r)
       =-1483/64+9c sqrt(32) sqrt(A(r)/r)>0.          (37)

Here A(r)>1 and r<1, c>1 and sqrt(32)>5, so the positive term is
greater than45 while 1483/64<24. At the left endpoint,

    A(1/4)=101/64,
    f(1/4)=153/202+18/sqrt(202)>2.                  (38)

The last exact comparison is equivalent to 18sqrt(202)>251; its
squared positive sides are 65448>63001. This contradicts (36), and
proves (35). All inequalities use the same two actual residual bodies
and their actual whole-body B sums; no independently attainable
marginal distributions are substituted.

## Scope

The conclusion rules out all hypothetical bad sources in this branch
with a>=b/6. It leaves an explicit small-A regime and does not eliminate
that regime. In particular it does not convert any qualitative compactness
threshold from another argument into a numerical one. Every normalization
above is a common determinant-one continuous coordinate change, preserves
the fiber labels, and tracks the whole swept set inside the middle fiber.
The source need not be a global maximizer over the mixed set.
With the additional two-residual condition a-u-w>0, the latest bound
is a<b/32. This still leaves a positive small-endpoint regime and is
not a complete exclusion of that regime.
